units.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
units.intro: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds Deepen Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds with definitions, worked examples, and exam tips in the cards below.

cards.title: 4.1.1 Physical Properties
body: Materials required: test substances (iron, copper, aluminium, magnesium or any other metal that is easily available), hammer, battery, light bulb, bulb holder and crocodile clips.
The crocodile clips should be connected to the battery and the light bulb should also be connected into the circuit.

cards.title: 4.1.2 Chemical Properties
body: Materials required: Sodium, magnesium, iron, copper, eye protection, water, seven test tubes, dilute hydrochloric acid, a pair tongs.
Always take very small pieces of sodium metal and handle them with the tongs.

cards.title: 4.1.3 Activity Series of Metals and Application in Metallurgy
body: A major source of metals and their compounds is the Earth’s crust.
The two most abundant elements in the earth’s crust are oxygen and silicon.

cards.title: Worked: metal displacement
cards.problem: Will Zn metal displace Cu²⁺ from CuSO₄(aq)? (Zn is above Cu in the activity series.)

steps.text: A more active metal reduces ions of a less active metal.
Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻; Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Net: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

cards.answer: Yes — copper metal plates out; the blue Cu²⁺ colour fades.

cards.title: Metals & compounds
body: Metals form cations; good conductors. Activity series ranks ease of oxidation.
Compounds: oxides, hydroxides, carbonates, salts — many industrial uses.

cards.title: Extraction idea
body: Reactive metals often from electrolysis; less reactive may be reduced by carbon.
Corrosion: metals oxidise (e.g. rusting of Fe needs water + O₂).

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds: checklist before exam
body: Can you define every bold term in **Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds** without looking?
Can you redo each worked example with the answer covered?
Can you sketch one diagram/graph/map and label it in under 2 minutes?

cards.title: Sodium and its Compounds
body: **Sodium and its Compounds.** Focus on the key definitions, formulas, and diagrams for this section.
Work one textbook example step by step, then close the book and reproduce the reasoning.
Then try the unit exercises below — check wrong options against the definitions before guessing.

cards.title: Sodium reacts with water
body: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Sodium floats, melts into a ball and moves about; the solution becomes alkaline (turns red litmus blue).

cards.title: Worked: rust conditions
cards.problem: Does iron rust in dry pure oxygen alone easily?

steps.text: Rusting needs both water and oxygen typically.

cards.answer: Moisture is required for ordinary rusting.

tips.text: Memorise a short activity list: K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au.
A metal above H in the series can liberate H₂ from dilute acids.

questions.q: The mineral from which copper is extracted is
why: Chalcopyrite (copper pyrites) CuFeS₂ is the main copper ore (textbook Table 4.2).
Magnetite Fe₃O₄ and haematite Fe₂O₃ → iron; galena PbS → lead; bauxite Al₂O₃·2H₂O → aluminium.
questions.tip: Read all the options before you choose; cross out the ones that belong to a different idea.

questions.q: In the reaction M(s) + 2HCl(aq) → H₂(g) + MCl₂(aq), M displaces hydrogen from the acid. M may stand for
why: Only metals above hydrogen in the activity series displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Cu, Hg and Pt are below hydrogen; Zn is above it: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Answer: C.
